convoLines.text: "We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Elena. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"Raul is gone and Consuelo is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"I greet everyone by name each morning. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"The fire feels smaller without Consuelo. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"I should get back to it."
"This was good." They mean it.
Desmond: "Can I ask you something? ... I want us to stick together. Properly. Watch each other's backs."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Common Sorrel — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
"This one — American Persimmon. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Consuelo is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Elena grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Desmond is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Stand beside them first — same side of the Haven door — then help.
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"I dreamed Consuelo was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sleep's gone strange. I taste the water before the others drink at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Desmond nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About who you left behind — Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Can I be honest? Still on who you left behind."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"About this wound — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"I still need help with this wound."
Wound care requires an untreated wound below 70 health and no current illness.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Raul owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ernesto is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"what's been happening — that's still where we are."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."

They nod. "Okay."
"a ridge with a view for miles — remember the shape of it. It's real, and it's worth knowing."
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
That could have stung. They let it pass — you've been kind before.
"Still on what you make of all this."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Raul died... I keep expecting to see Raul at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ernesto nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Desmond sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Desmond shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
"No, no — just asking. Idle curiosity, I swear."
"Oh! Still on whether you're staying."
"Alright — I should get back to it."

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — what you make of all this, settled. Feels better said out loud."

"I still need a hand with this wound."

"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"

"Okay. We'll pick this up later."

"Groups have gravity. They pull you into their problems. I stay in my own orbit."

"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"I keep thinking about that The Bailiff. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"Promise me that. Please."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."

"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that news I was bursting to share — You'll never guess what I saw by the treeline."
"The treeline, this morning — something moved out there, big. By the time I looked properly it was gone. But I saw it."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Oh." A long pause. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Omaha, Nebraska. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others." Liv won't meet your eyes.
"Have you been thinking about the truth I told you? Because I have. A lot."
"It's just — Still on that news."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Raul Fontana is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Raul is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Raul Fontana is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Raul kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Raul's gone." Desmond looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Raul." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Gus blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 1). Red sky at night, shepherd's delight. Red sky at morning, shepherd's warning. It works.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Cordage (Level 1). Twist plant fibers into string. Dogbane, nettle, yucca — strong fibers are everywhere.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Raul Fontana, 41 days. The mantle passes to Gus ODonnell.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Gus ODonnell, 36 — a farmer. Their hands know different work now: Bloodhound, Lucky Rock, Green Whisper, Night Eyes, Trophy Room.
d41: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Stalker of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Raul — and Raul is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Consuelo, Ernesto, Desmond and 1 more speak for Gus — "Raul trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Gus before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
